---
title: "Optimal reports along the withholding-cost path"
subtitle: "2.5 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 11 and 16"
description: "The lower envelope of affine report-risk functions and its change points."
---

The risk of a fixed report changes linearly with the withholding cost. The slope is the share of pairs the report withholds. The lowest line at each τ gives the smallest risk in the selected family. Where the lowest line changes, the reports on either side of that point tie. A cap on the number of grades can remove some of these reports and change the path. The low-cost view shows the first transitions, including the range over which the best report withholds every pair.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Overview.** The unrestricted best report states 14 pairs, with risk .0372. The capped comparison gives .0417.
  Each faint line gives the risk of a fixed report. The heavy line traces the lowest risk, and the bands below show the costs over which each report attains it. Arrow keys identify the reports on the envelope. Complete path gives their exact intervals.
- **Before the first bend.** The report states 0 of 15 pairs, and risk equals the withholding cost .0005. The
  low-cost strip includes the all-withheld report that an overview starting farther right would miss. The
  left boundary is a limit, since the cost is positive.
- **Small cost, coherent report.** The best report states 12 of 15 pairs, including 2 directions whose error
  exceeds the withholding cost. The list under Complete path gives the error probability for each newly stated direction. These choices are
  made jointly, so the path cannot be read as a collection of isolated-pair thresholds.
- **Exactly at a bend.** 2 reports share the smallest risk. Both neighboring segments include the
  shared endpoint; the read-out shows the first report under the stated equal-risk tolerance. Moving just
  beyond the bend changes which line is lowest.
- **Three-grade cap.** At the larger cost the capped report still states 12 of 15 pairs, with risk .0817; the
  unrestricted comparison gives .0480. Restricting the available grades changes the decision problem even
  though the posterior and the price of withholding are the same.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The site posteriors are normal and specified for this example. A separate panel shows targets with equal means. In that example, some reports minimize risk at a single cost. The path includes them even though they occupy no interval of positive length.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- c(A=1L,B=2L,C=3L,D=3L,E=4L,F=5L)
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$weighted_risk # .03717176
```
The call evaluates the displayed report at a fixed cost.
:::

Standalone: [the τ path](../../embed/tau-path.html), for example `?tau=.005&zoom=low`.
